page.layout: One page part, shown only as the left part of the scan: at the top a decorative ornament, then a large title line cut at the right edge ("I" over "LOCOR"), a centred italic line "Quæ in", and an italic line "Prior Num". Below is a two-column list of locations, its column of references running to the right edge: "GENI..." heading over reference lines, a gap, a second group of "v." lines, a gap, then "EXO..." heading over reference lines.; One page block: ornamental woodcut header at top; below it a title block of four centred lines; then a right-aligned column of page and section references, with a short heading "...ESIS." and a second heading "...DUS." followed by more references. No margins with text.; Header ornament across the top; title lines in capitals and a subtitle line; a few lines of text below; then one narrow column of index references on the left, with two cross-headings (LEVITICUS, NUMERI) set between the groups; a page number beside one line.; One column of references at the right, with fragments of entry text at the left edge (cut off); top: fragment of a title and entry words, then reference lines running down; catchword at the foot right. No running head or page number.
page.notes: The right-hand part of the title and reference lines is cut off in this part; the visible text ends where the image ends. The gap between the reference groups is blank space, and the two headings "GENI" and "EXO" continue beyond the cut. "v. 11, 12.13" is copied as printed; the comma after 11 is as it appears in the scan. Top title lines are cut off at the left edge; only their final letters are visible. The heading LEVITICUS is cut short on the right; the NUMERI heading is doubtful at its end. Left edge of the strip is cut, so entry words at the start of lines are missing; "3. t. 10. & 11" and the fragments "US." and "RI." are cut-off remnants and may be incomplete. The top fragment "URÆ," is the end of a title word. Reading of small numerals (e.g. "41", "599") is from the scan and may be uncertain.
